chapter: Emmett Hardy and the river towns
title: Pansy Lane's band and the Pluto Blues at the Grunewald cave
summary: He says he never played with the elder Lane but did with Pansy, and tells of the band's stunt at the hotel cave.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: You ever played any of his bands? No, I never did.

I played in his son's bands. I played, played in, don't call him Pansy cause I'm kidding. Yeah, I know. I played in his bands. I never did play in the old man's bands. I guess I'm one of the few guys that never did. I know him quite well, but I never did play with him. Raymond played with him. Yeah. But I played with Pansy quite a bit. Did Raymond ever tell you a story about Pansy's band at the Roosevelt Hotel? Was he at the Grunwald Hotel then?
Was it, uh, would it make any difference if this was a little disc game? No, no, no.
Say anything you want. Tell me.

Well they, they, they had a place in the Grunwald, which is the Roosevelt now. They had a place in there called a cave. It was underneath the, where the kitchen is now. See. And how, how, how Pansy and them got the job I don't know. Because there was a raggedy band. You know, I mean, they didn't. They didn't, they were all guys from around the channel and downtown like that, that, and, uh, weren't the best dressed in town, you know. But they got the job anyway, and they had a tune they used to do called the Poo Toe Blues. And the climax of the, of the thing was that, uh, Pansy would, uh, they'd make a break, you see, and Pansy would go, you know, like that. And the drummer would roll out a, a roll of toilet flipper, you know, and everybody would holler, ooh, the Pluto Blues. And then, they'd pull this stunt, this, this, this, the only high class job they ever got, you see. That's the Roosevelt. And then, and then, and then, they, they pulled this stunt, you know, with the Pluto Blues, and then, uh, they run, they run completely out of the hotel. I thought maybe Raymond would tell you about the guy. I think Raymond was there.
